DATA_DIR_CANDIDATES = [Path("Dataset"), Path.cwd() / "Dataset", Path.cwd()]
DATA_DIR = next(
    (
        folder
        for folder in DATA_DIR_CANDIDATES
        if (folder / "Customer_Master_Data.csv").exists()
        and (folder / "Customer_Transactions.csv").exists()
    ),
    None,
)

if DATA_DIR is None:
    searched_paths = ", ".join(str(folder) for folder in DATA_DIR_CANDIDATES)
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Dataset files were not found. Expected Customer_Master_Data.csv and "
        f"Customer_Transactions.csv in one of: {searched_paths}"
    )

CUSTOMER_FILE = DATA_DIR / "Customer_Master_Data.csv"
CUSTOMER_XLSX_FILE = DATA_DIR / "Customer_Master_Data.xlsx"
TRANSACTION_FILE = DATA_DIR / "Customer_Transactions.csv"

The first code cells import the customer and transaction files, then check basic structure, sample rows, unique customers, data types, and consistency between the provided CSV/XLSX customer master files.

df_customers_raw = pd.read_csv(CUSTOMER_FILE)
df_transactions_raw = pd.read_csv(TRANSACTION_FILE)

xlsx_status = "Not provided"
if CUSTOMER_XLSX_FILE.exists():
    df_customers_xlsx = pd.read_excel(CUSTOMER_XLSX_FILE)
    csv_compare = df_customers_raw.copy()
    xlsx_compare = df_customers_xlsx.copy()
    for frame in (csv_compare, xlsx_compare):
        frame["JoinDate"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["JoinDate"], errors="coerce").dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        for column in frame.select_dtypes(include=["object", "string"]).columns:
            frame[column] = frame[column].astype("string").str.strip()
    xlsx_status = "Matches CSV after date normalization" if csv_compare.equals(xlsx_compare) else "Does not match CSV"

load_summary = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Dataset": ["Customer master", "Transactions"],

        "Unique CustomerIDs": [
            df_customers_raw["CustomerID"].nunique(),
            df_transactions_raw["CustomerID"].nunique(),
        ],
    }
)

artifact_summary = pd.DataFrame(

Cleaned Data¶

In [4]:
df_customers = df_customers_raw.copy()
df_transactions = df_transactions_raw.copy()


def clean_text_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = df.copy()
    text_columns = df.select_dtypes(include=["object", "string"]).columns
    for column in text_columns:
        df[column] = (
            df[column]
            .astype("string")
            .str.strip()
            .replace({"": pd.NA, "nan": pd.NA, "None": pd.NA, "NaN": pd.NA})
        )
    return df


df_customers = clean_text_columns(df_customers)
df_transactions = clean_text_columns(df_transactions)

df_customers["Age"] = pd.to_numeric(df_customers["Age"], errors="coerce")
df_customers["NumChildren"] = pd.to_numeric(df_customers["NumChildren"], errors="coerce")
df_customers["JoinDate"] = pd.to_datetime(df_customers["JoinDate"], format="%Y-%m-%d", errors="coerce")
df_transactions["TransactionDate"] = pd.to_datetime(df_transactions["TransactionDate"], format="%m/%d/%y", errors="coerce")
df_transactions["TransactionAmount"] = pd.to_numeric(
    df_transactions["TransactionAmount"], errors="coerce"
)

valid_genders = {"Male", "Female", "Not Disclosed"}
valid_marital_status = {"Single", "Married", "Divorced", "Widowed"}
customer_id_pattern = r"^CUST\d{5}$"
email_pattern = r"^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$"

transaction_join_audit = df_transactions.merge(
    df_customers[["CustomerID", "JoinDate"]], on="CustomerID", how="left"
)

quality_checks_before = {
    "Customer rows": len(df_customers),
    "Transaction rows": len(df_transactions),
    "Customer duplicate IDs": int(df_customers.duplicated("CustomerID").sum()),
    "Exact duplicate customer rows": int(df_customers.duplicated().sum()),
    "Exact duplicate transaction rows": int(df_transactions.duplicated().sum()),
    "Missing customer cells": int(df_customers.isna().sum().sum()),
    "Missing transaction cells": int(df_transactions.isna().sum().sum()),
    "Invalid customer ID format": int((~df_customers["CustomerID"].str.match(customer_id_pattern, na=False)).sum()),
    "Invalid transaction customer ID format": int((~df_transactions["CustomerID"].str.match(customer_id_pattern, na=False)).sum()),
    "Invalid email values": int((~df_customers["Email"].str.match(email_pattern, na=False)).sum()),
    "Invalid customer JoinDate": int(df_customers["JoinDate"].isna().sum()),
    "Invalid transaction date": int(df_transactions["TransactionDate"].isna().sum()),
    "Invalid or non-positive transaction amount": int(
        (df_transactions["TransactionAmount"].isna() | (df_transactions["TransactionAmount"] <= 0)).sum()
    ),
    "Age outside 18-75": int((df_customers["Age"].isna() | ~df_customers["Age"].between(18, 75)).sum()),
    "Invalid NumChildren values": int(
        (
            df_customers["NumChildren"].isna()
            | (df_customers["NumChildren"] < 0)
            | (df_customers["NumChildren"] % 1 != 0)
        ).sum()
    ),
    "Invalid gender values": int((~df_customers["Gender"].isin(valid_genders)).sum()),
    "Invalid marital status values": int(
        (~df_customers["MaritalStatus"].isin(valid_marital_status)).sum()
    ),
    "Transaction CustomerIDs not in master": int(
        (~df_transactions["CustomerID"].isin(df_customers["CustomerID"])).sum()
    ),
    "Transactions before customer JoinDate": int(
        (transaction_join_audit["TransactionDate"] < transaction_join_audit["JoinDate"]).sum()
    ),
}

In [5]:
customer_rows_before = len(df_customers)
transaction_rows_before = len(df_transactions)

df_customers_clean = (
    df_customers.drop_duplicates()
    .drop_duplicates(subset=["CustomerID"], keep="first")
    .copy()
)

required_customer_columns = [
    "CustomerID", "Name", "Email", "Gender", "Age", "City",
    "MaritalStatus", "NumChildren", "JoinDate"
]
df_customers_clean = df_customers_clean.dropna(subset=required_customer_columns).copy()
df_customers_clean = df_customers_clean[
    df_customers_clean["CustomerID"].str.match(customer_id_pattern, na=False)
    & df_customers_clean["Email"].str.match(email_pattern, na=False)
    & df_customers_clean["Age"].between(18, 75)
    & (df_customers_clean["NumChildren"] >= 0)
    & (df_customers_clean["NumChildren"] % 1 == 0)
    & df_customers_clean["Gender"].isin(valid_genders)
    & df_customers_clean["MaritalStatus"].isin(valid_marital_status)
].copy()
df_customers_clean["Age"] = df_customers_clean["Age"].astype(int)
df_customers_clean["NumChildren"] = df_customers_clean["NumChildren"].astype(int)

df_transactions_clean = df_transactions.drop_duplicates().copy()
df_transactions_clean = df_transactions_clean.dropna(
    subset=["CustomerID", "TransactionDate", "TransactionAmount"]
).copy()
df_transactions_clean = df_transactions_clean[
    df_transactions_clean["CustomerID"].str.match(customer_id_pattern, na=False)
].copy()
df_transactions_clean = df_transactions_clean[df_transactions_clean["TransactionAmount"] > 0].copy()
df_transactions_clean = df_transactions_clean[
    df_transactions_clean["CustomerID"].isin(df_customers_clean["CustomerID"])
].copy()
df_transactions_clean = df_transactions_clean.merge(
    df_customers_clean[["CustomerID", "JoinDate"]], on="CustomerID", how="left"
)
df_transactions_clean = df_transactions_clean[
    df_transactions_clean["TransactionDate"] >= df_transactions_clean["JoinDate"]
].drop(columns="JoinDate").copy()

cleaning_summary = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Dataset": ["Customer master", "Transactions"],
        "Rows before": [customer_rows_before, transaction_rows_before],
        "Rows after": [len(df_customers_clean), len(df_transactions_clean)],
        "Rows removed": [
            customer_rows_before - len(df_customers_clean),
            transaction_rows_before - len(df_transactions_clean),
        ],
    }
)

display(cleaning_summary)
Dataset Rows before Rows after Rows removed

1 Transactions 23050 23050 0

Customer Transactions¶

In [7]:
df_merged = df_transactions_clean.merge(df_customers_clean, on="CustomerID", how="left")

age_bins = [17, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75]
age_labels = ["18-25", "26-35", "36-45", "46-55", "56-65", "66-75"]
df_customers_clean["AgeGroup"] = pd.cut(
    df_customers_clean["Age"], bins=age_bins, labels=age_labels, include_lowest=True
)
df_merged["AgeGroup"] = pd.cut(
    df_merged["Age"], bins=age_bins, labels=age_labels, include_lowest=True
)

customer_spend = (
    df_transactions_clean.groupby("CustomerID", as_index=False)
    .agg(TotalSpend=("TransactionAmount", "sum"), Transactions=("TransactionAmount", "count"))
)
df_customer_profile = df_customers_clean.merge(customer_spend, on="CustomerID", how="left")
df_customer_profile["TotalSpend"] = df_customer_profile["TotalSpend"].fillna(0)
df_customer_profile["Transactions"] = df_customer_profile["Transactions"].fillna(0).astype(int)
spend_pct_rank = df_customer_profile["TotalSpend"].rank(method="average", pct=True)
df_customer_profile["SpendBracket"] = pd.cut(
    spend_pct_rank,
    bins=[0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00],
    labels=["Low", "Medium", "High", "Very High"],
    include_lowest=True,
)

merge_summary = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Metric": [
            "Merged rows",
            "Merged columns",
            "Unique customers in merged data",
            "Total transaction revenue",
            "Average transaction amount",
            "Median transaction amount",
        ],
        "Value": [
            len(df_merged),
            df_merged.shape[1],
            df_merged["CustomerID"].nunique(),
            round(df_merged["TransactionAmount"].sum(), 2),
            round(df_merged["TransactionAmount"].mean(), 2),
            round(df_merged["TransactionAmount"].median(), 2),
        ],
    }
)

Customer Scoring¶

In [12]:
def quintile_score(series: pd.Series, high_is_good: bool = True) -> pd.Series:
    ranked = series.rank(method="first", ascending=True)
    labels = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] if high_is_good else [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
    return pd.qcut(ranked, q=5, labels=labels).astype(int)


df_rfm["R_Score"] = quintile_score(df_rfm["Recency"], high_is_good=False)
df_rfm["F_Score"] = quintile_score(df_rfm["Frequency"], high_is_good=True)
df_rfm["M_Score"] = quintile_score(df_rfm["Monetary"], high_is_good=True)

score_weights = np.asarray(matlib.matrix([[1, 1, 1]])).ravel()
df_rfm["RFM_Total"] = (
    df_rfm[["R_Score", "F_Score", "M_Score"]].to_numpy() * score_weights
).sum(axis=1).astype(int)

In [14]:
segment_priority_note = (
    "Segment rules are evaluated from top to bottom. At Risk is intentionally checked before "
    "Loyal Customers because poor recency is treated as a retention risk even when frequency is high."
)
display(Markdown(f"**Segment rule priority:** {segment_priority_note}"))


def assign_segment(row) -> str:
    r, f, m = int(row["R_Score"]), int(row["F_Score"]), int(row["M_Score"])
    if r >= 4 and f >= 4 and m >= 4:
        return "Champions"
    if r <= 2 and f >= 3:
        return "At Risk"
    if f >= 4 and r >= 2:
        return "Loyal Customers"
    if r >= 4 and f == 1:
        return "New Customers"
    if m >= 4 and 2 <= f <= 3 and r >= 3:
        return "Big Spenders"
    if r >= 4 and 2 <= f <= 3:
        return "Potential Loyalists"
    if r == 1 and f <= 2 and m <= 2:
        return "Lost"
    if r <= 2 and f <= 2:
        return "Hibernating"
    if r == 3 and f >= 3:
        return "Need Attention"
    return "Promising"


df_rfm["Segment"] = df_rfm.apply(assign_segment, axis=1)

segment_summary = (
    df_rfm.groupby("Segment", as_index=False)
    .agg(
        Customers=("CustomerID", "nunique"),
        Revenue=("Monetary", "sum"),
        AvgRecency=("Recency", "mean"),
        AvgFrequency=("Frequency", "mean"),
        AvgMonetary=("Monetary", "mean"),
        AvgRFMTotal=("RFM_Total", "mean"),
    )
    .sort_values("Revenue", ascending=False)
)
segment_summary["Customer Share %"] = segment_summary["Customers"] / segment_summary["Customers"].sum() * 100
segment_summary["Revenue Share %"] = segment_summary["Revenue"] / segment_summary["Revenue"].sum() * 100

display(segment_summary)

High-Value Customer Contribution¶

In [18]:
df_pareto = df_rfm.sort_values("Monetary", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
df_pareto["CustomerRank"] = np.arange(1, len(df_pareto) + 1)
df_pareto["CumulativeRevenue"] = df_pareto["Monetary"].cumsum()
df_pareto["CumulativeRevenuePct"] = df_pareto["CumulativeRevenue"] / df_pareto["Monetary"].sum() * 100
df_pareto["CustomerPct"] = df_pareto["CustomerRank"] / len(df_pareto) * 100

top_20_count = math.ceil(len(df_pareto) * 0.20)
top_20_share = df_pareto.iloc[top_20_count - 1]["CumulativeRevenuePct"]

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 7))
ax1.bar(df_pareto["CustomerRank"], df_pareto["Monetary"], color="#9ecae1", alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel("Customers Ranked by Monetary Value")
ax1.set_ylabel("Customer Monetary Value (INR)")
ax1.set_title(f"Pareto Analysis - Top 20% Customers Contribute {top_20_share:.1f}% of Revenue")

ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.plot(df_pareto["CustomerRank"], df_pareto["CumulativeRevenuePct"], color="#de2d26", linewidth=2.5)
ax2.axvline(top_20_count, color="#31a354", linestyle="--", label="Top 20% customers")
ax2.axhline(top_20_share, color="#756bb1", linestyle="--", label=f"{top_20_share:.1f}% revenue")
ax2.axhline(80, color="#636363", linestyle=":", label="80% reference")
ax2.set_ylabel("Cumulative Revenue %")
ax2.set_ylim(0, 105)
ax2.legend(loc="lower right")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Business Highlights¶

  • The cleaned dataset contains 1,000 customers, 23,050 transactions, and INR 23,053,199.66 in total revenue.
  • The average transaction amount is INR 1,000.14.
  • The strongest revenue segment is At Risk, contributing 25.3% of revenue.
  • The largest segment by customer count is At Risk, representing 22.8% of customers.
  • Champions: 130 customers and 16.5% of revenue. Use early access offers, premium bundles, loyalty rewards, and referral campaigns for this group.
  • At Risk: 228 customers and 25.3% of revenue. Use personalized win-back offers, reminders, and reactivation messages.
  • Top revenue city is Lucknow, with INR 2,609,437.63 revenue from 110 customers.
  • The strongest age group by revenue is 36-45. Tailor campaigns and product recommendations to this cohort.
  • The top 20% of customers contribute 27.0% of revenue. This dataset does not follow the classic 80/20 Pareto pattern; revenue is fairly spread, so campaigns should support both high-value customers and regular repeat buyers.
  • Segment labeling uses priority-based rules: At Risk is evaluated before Loyal Customers to flag frequent but stale buyers for retention.

Recommended Marketing Actions¶

  • Champions: Prioritize early access offers, loyalty rewards, referral benefits, and premium bundles.
  • Loyal Customers: Use reward points, product bundles, personalized upsell, and membership offers.
  • Potential Loyalists: Use second-purchase coupons, product recommendations, and onboarding journeys.
  • New Customers: Send welcome offers, education messages, and next-best-product recommendations.
  • Big Spenders: Recommend premium products, provide better support, and nurture loyalty.
  • At Risk: Send personalized win-back offers, reminders, and feedback requests.
  • Hibernating: Use limited-time offers and lightweight reactivation campaigns.
  • Lost: Use low-cost reactivation messages only; avoid heavy discount spend.
  • Need Attention: Send targeted reminders and moderate incentives before they become at-risk customers.
  • Promising: Nurture with product discovery, low-cost coupons, and campaigns that increase purchase frequency.

Suggestion¶

  • For future analysis, the company should collect additional fields such as income range, preferred product category, campaign response, and customer feedback. These details can make customer targeting more accurate and improve future marketing recommendations.
